title: The complex couplings
claim: Counting on the knot's spaces is #P-hard at every complex coupling lam0 outside {0, 1, -1, -3} (and polynomial at those and at lam = oo). The ratios of the Fano atom and of the 12-incidence splice class define an irreducible curve of bidegree (13, 7) that is not a torsion coset; by Beukers and Smyth its torsion points lie on seven resultants, whose only cyclotomic factors are Phi_1 and Phi_2, so its torsion points are exactly (1, 1) and (-1, -1), reached only at lam = oo and lam = 0. Where one ratio is 0 or infinite the other has infinite order, except at lam = +-1. So at every other lam0 one of the two atoms meets the hypothesis of Theorem 1 of ticket B. With one line deleted the same holds except at lam = -3 (left open): the six line-deleted Fano atoms degenerate together only at lam = 1.
failure_conditions: A torsion point of the curve other than (1, 1) and (-1, -1), or a missed cyclotomic factor of a resultant.
A zero or pole of one ratio at which the other ratio is 0, infinite or a root of unity, other than lam = +-1.
A multiplicative relation between the two ratios.
foundation_claim_scope: Completes the coupling dichotomy on the knot's spaces over the complex numbers.

validation.status: checked: the ratios against ticket A; the curve's irreducibility; the seven Beukers-Smyth resultants and their cyclotomic factors (finite-field filter, exact confirmation); the torsion points; their couplings; zeros and poles; the deficiency-one atoms; controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: torsion points on curves (Lang; Ihara, Serre, Tate; Beukers-Smyth) are classical; their use to close a counting dichotomy on a restricted class is routine in spirit (Cai and coauthors use similar algebraic independence arguments); the statement for the knot's spaces: no overlap found yet
